subject: mathematics
question_text: If cos θ + sin θ = √2 cos θ, prove that cos θ − sin θ = √2 sin θ.

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), chapter 8 TRIGONOMETRIC RATIOS, Very Short Answer question 10, book p.84. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The 1+1 split rewards the rearrangement sin θ = (√2 − 1) cos θ first and the regrouping 2 − √2 = √2(√2 − 1) second, which are the two moves the proof is made of. Paper position: Maths-1A Section A runs Q1 to Q10 at 2 marks each, all compulsory, under the 2026-27 pattern; Trigonometric Ratios and Transformations holds two of those ten slots. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Checked numerically: the given relation forces tan θ = √2 − 1, so θ = 22½°; there cos θ + sin θ and √2 cos θ are both 1.3065629649, and cos θ − sin θ and √2 sin θ are both 0.5411961001. The other branch θ = 202½° was checked too and both sides agree there as well. The proof never squares, so no sign branch has to be chosen anywhere.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this one — what you do with the given relation, and how the √2 comes back out.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Rearrange the given relation
steps.margin_note: First mark. The given relation already links sin θ and cos θ, so it only has to be rearranged. Nothing is squared, so no sign case appears later.
steps.memory_tip: Move cos θ across, not sin θ. That leaves sin θ = (√2 − 1) cos θ, which is the only fact the proof uses.
lines: Given cos θ + sin θ = √2 cos θ.
If cos θ were 0, the given relation would
force sin θ = 0 too, so cos θ ≠ 0.
Take cos θ across to the right side:
sin θ = √2 cos θ − cos θ

recall.must_convey: That the given relation is rearranged to sin θ = (√2 − 1) cos θ.
accept: take cos theta to the other side so sin theta is root two minus one times cos theta
rearrange the given to get sin theta in terms of cos theta
sin theta equals root two minus one into cos theta
cos theta ni transfer chesi sin theta equals root two minus one cos theta rasta
shift cos theta and factor it out

steps.why: The given relation is already a link between sin θ and cos θ, so rearranging it is enough. Squaring would introduce a sign choice that this question does not need, and cos θ cannot be 0 because that would force sin θ to be 0 as well.
common_mistakes: Squaring the given relation instead of rearranging it.
Writing sin θ = (1 − √2) cos θ with the signs the wrong way round.

steps.label: Take out √2 and finish
steps.margin_note: Second mark. 2 − √2 = √2(√2 − 1), and (√2 − 1) cos θ is sin θ by line (1). That single regrouping ends the proof.
steps.memory_tip: 2 − √2 = √2(√2 − 1). The bracket (√2 − 1) cos θ is exactly sin θ from line (1).
lines: cos θ − sin θ = cos θ − (√2 − 1) cos θ

lines.text: ∴ cos θ − sin θ = √2 sin θ

recall.must_convey: That 2 − √2 is written as √2(√2 − 1), and (√2 − 1) cos θ is replaced by sin θ.
accept: two minus root two is root two times root two minus one so it becomes root two sin theta
take root two out and the bracket is sin theta again
substitute line one back and get root two sin theta
two minus root two ni root two bracket root two minus one ga rasta
the bracket root two minus one cos theta is sin theta

steps.why: The factor 2 − √2 is √2(√2 − 1), and (√2 − 1) cos θ is sin θ by line (1). That one regrouping is the whole proof, and since nothing was squared no sign has to be chosen.
common_mistakes: Writing 2 − √2 as √2(1 − √2), which has the wrong sign.
Stopping at (2 − √2) cos θ without turning it into √2 sin θ.
